name: The Sacred Valley
tagline: The Inca Empire's agricultural heartland, a fertile Andean valley strung with ruins, living villages and genuinely extraordinary engineering.
highlight: Standing at the rim of Moray's perfectly concentric circular terraces, each level once its own distinct microclimate for testing crops.
shortDescription: The Inca Empire's fertile agricultural heartland, a valley of ruins, salt pans and living villages between Cusco and Machu Picchu.
metaDescription: A Sacred Valley travel guide: Pisac, Ollantaytambo, Moray, the Maras salt mines, food and how to plan a visit to Peru's Inca heartland.
nearestAirport: Alejandro Velasco Astete International Airport (CUZ), via Cusco
knownFor: Inca ruins, the Maras salt mines, living Andean villages

intro: The Sacred Valley is genuinely the Inca Empire's agricultural heartland, a fertile stretch of the Urubamba River valley that fed Cusco and supported some of the empire's most sophisticated engineering.

Its villages are genuinely still living Andean communities, not just open-air museums, with Ollantaytambo in particular retaining its original Inca street grid, still inhabited after more than 500 years.

Most visitors genuinely pass through en route between Cusco and Machu Picchu, though the valley's own sites — Pisac, Ollantaytambo, Moray and the Maras salt pans — easily reward a dedicated day or two, and its lower altitude makes it a genuinely useful acclimatisation stop.

whyVisit.intro: The Sacred Valley's case rests on genuinely combining major Inca sites with living Andean culture and a gentler altitude.

points.title: Ollantaytambo is genuinely still a living Inca town
points.text: Its original street grid and water channels remain in daily use after more than 500 years.

points.title: Moray's terraces are genuinely a feat of agricultural science
points.text: Concentric circular terraces once used to test crops across distinct microclimates.

points.title: The Maras salt pans are genuinely still worked by hand
points.text: Thousands of individual pools, harvested using techniques unchanged for centuries.

points.title: Pisac combines genuinely major ruins with an excellent market
points.text: Impressive Inca terracing above town, and one of the region's best craft markets below.

points.title: It's genuinely lower altitude than Cusco
points.text: A useful, gentler stop for acclimatising before higher-altitude activities.

attractionsIntro: The valley's essential sights combine major Inca ruins with genuinely still-living Andean villages and landscapes.

attractions.name: Pisac ruins

image.file: File:Peru - Sacred Valley & Incan Ruins 217 - Pisac (8114883162).jpg
image.alt: The Inca ruins above the town of Pisac

attractions.text: Genuinely impressive Inca terracing and ceremonial structures on a ridge high above the town, among the valley's most significant sites.
attractions.tip: Genuinely arrive early to explore the ruins before the midday tour groups arrive.

attractions.name: Pisac market

image.alt: The market in Pisac in the Sacred Valley

attractions.text: Genuinely one of the region's best craft markets, textiles, ceramics and jewellery sold in the town square below the ruins.
attractions.tip: Genuinely Sunday brings the largest and most authentic version of the market.

attractions.name: Ollantaytambo fortress

image.alt: The Inca fortress terraces at Ollantaytambo

attractions.text: Genuinely a massive terraced fortress, the site of one of the few battles the Inca actually won against the invading Spanish.
attractions.tip: Genuinely the steep climb to the top is rewarded with sweeping views over the whole town.

attractions.name: Ollantaytambo town

image.alt: The living Inca town of Ollantaytambo

attractions.text: Genuinely the valley's best-preserved living Inca town, its original street grid and stone water channels still in daily use.
attractions.tip: Genuinely wander the back streets away from the fortress for the town's most authentic atmosphere.

attractions.name: Moray

image.alt: The circular terraces of Moray in the Sacred Valley

attractions.text: Genuinely a remarkable feat of Inca agricultural science, concentric circular terraces creating distinct microclimates believed to have tested crops.
attractions.tip: Genuinely the temperature difference between the terraces' top and bottom levels is real and noticeable.

attractions.name: The Maras salt mines

image.file: File:Salineras de Maras, Maras, Perú, 2015-07-30, DD 12.JPG
image.alt: The Maras salt pans in the Sacred Valley

attractions.text: Genuinely thousands of individual salt pools cascading down a hillside, fed by a natural spring and harvested by hand since Inca times.
attractions.tip: Genuinely combine with a Moray visit, since both sit close together on the valley's northern side.

attractions.name: Chinchero

image.file: File:Site archéologique de Chinchero et Plaza de Chinchero en 2011.jpg
image.alt: The archaeological site and plaza at Chinchero

attractions.text: Genuinely a traditional weaving village with its own Inca ruins and a striking colonial church built directly atop an Inca palace.
attractions.tip: Genuinely check out a local weaving demonstration, showing techniques passed down for generations.

thingsToDoIntro: The valley genuinely rewards a full day or two combining ruins, markets and genuine Andean village life.

thingsToDo.title: Browse Pisac's artisan market

image.alt: Crafts for sale at Pisac market

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely relaxed way to spend a morning, browsing textiles and crafts from across the wider region.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely polite bargaining is expected and normal here.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Ollantaytambo's fortress terraces

image.alt: Climbing the fortress terraces at Ollantaytambo

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely rewarding, if steep, climb through massive terraces to the fortress's upper ceremonial sector.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely take it slowly — the climb is more strenuous than it first appears at altitude.

thingsToDo.title: Walk Moray's circular terraces

image.alt: Walking down into Moray's circular terraces

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely striking descent into the terraces' concentric rings, appreciating the engineering up close.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely combine with the nearby Maras salt pans for a full half-day out from Cusco.

thingsToDo.title: Photograph the Maras salt pans

image.file: File:Salineras de Maras, Maras, Perú, 2015-07-30, DD 09.JPG
image.alt: The terraced salt pans at Maras

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely striking sight, thousands of small pools glinting white and gold across the hillside.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely stay on the marked paths — the pans themselves are still actively worked by local families.

thingsToDo.title: Visit Chinchero's colonial church
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely striking blend of cultures, a Spanish colonial church built directly on Inca foundations, its interior richly painted.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely photography is often restricted inside the church itself — check current rules on arrival.

thingsToDo.title: Wander Ollantaytambo's living Inca streets

image.alt: Walking the Inca streets of Ollantaytambo

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely rare chance to walk streets still following their original Inca layout, water still running through centuries-old channels.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely a quiet early morning walk here feels genuinely different from the daytime tour crowds.

image.alt: Lomo saltado, a Peruvian stir-fry of beef, onions and fries

foods.text: A genuinely reliable classic found on menus throughout the valley's towns.

foods.name: Cuy (guinea pig)
foods.text: Genuinely a traditional Andean delicacy, especially associated with the valley's rural communities.
foods.whereToTry: Traditional restaurants throughout Pisac and Urubamba.

foods.name: Chicha morada
foods.text: Genuinely a refreshing, non-alcoholic purple corn drink found throughout the region, sweetened with fruit and spices.
foods.whereToTry: Restaurants and markets throughout the valley.

foods.name: Ceviche

image.alt: Ceviche, Peru's national dish of citrus-cured raw fish

foods.text: Genuinely available even this far inland, though a treat best saved for the coast.
foods.whereToTry: Peruvian restaurants throughout the valley's main towns.

foods.name: Pisco sour

image.alt: A pisco sour, Peru's national cocktail

foods.text: Genuinely a fitting way to end a day of exploring the valley's ruins and villages.
foods.whereToTry: Restaurants and bars throughout Ollantaytambo and Urubamba.

foods.name: Coca tea
foods.text: Genuinely useful for managing altitude symptoms, widely available throughout the valley.
foods.whereToTry: Hotels and cafés throughout the Sacred Valley.

options.detail: Regular services connect Cusco to Pisac, Urubamba and Ollantaytambo.

options.text: Genuinely the most flexible way to combine Pisac, Moray, Maras and Ollantaytambo.
options.detail: Roads throughout the valley are generally well maintained.

options.text: Genuinely easy — Pisac, Ollantaytambo and Chinchero are all small and walkable.

bestTime.headline: May to September for the dry season, though the valley works well year-round
bestTime.summary: The Sacred Valley is genuinely visitable in any season, given its slightly lower, milder altitude than Cusco.

seasons.text: Genuinely the most reliable weather for exploring the valley's outdoor ruins and terraces.
Genuinely fewer crowds with still-decent weather odds.
Genuinely lush and green, with the valley's agricultural roots on full display, though afternoon rain is common.

bestTime.avoid: Nothing strongly — the valley's genuinely lower altitude makes it a comfortable stop in any season.

days.title: Ollantaytambo, Moray and Maras

days.afternoon: Ollantaytambo's fortress and living Inca streets.
days.evening: Onward train to Machu Picchu, or dinner in Ollantaytambo.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Sacred Valley visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Buy genuinely the Boleto Turístico ahead if planning to visit Pisac and Ollantaytambo's ruins.
Combine genuinely Moray and the Maras salt pans in one trip, since they sit close together.
Book genuinely your onward Machu Picchu train from Ollantaytambo well ahead in peak season.
Wear genuinely comfortable shoes for the valley's uneven ruins and cobbled streets.
Consider genuinely basing yourself here for a night or two to help acclimatise before higher-altitude activities.
Bring genuinely small cash for Pisac's market and rural stalls throughout the valley.

faq.q: How many days do you need in the Sacred Valley?
faq.a: Two days genuinely covers Pisac, Ollantaytambo, Moray and the Maras salt pans comfortably.

faq.q: Is the Sacred Valley worth visiting separately from Machu Picchu?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — its own sites, especially Ollantaytambo and Moray, are significant enough to justify dedicated time.

faq.q: Can you use the Sacred Valley to help with altitude acclimatisation?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — it sits notably lower than Cusco, making it a useful, gentler stop before higher-altitude activities.

faq.q: What is the Sacred Valley known for?
faq.a: Genuinely being the Inca Empire's agricultural heartland, home to major ruins, the Maras salt pans and still-living traditional villages.

faq.q: Is Ollantaytambo really still an Inca town?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — its original Inca street grid and water channels remain in daily use, making it one of South America's oldest continuously inhabited urban layouts.

faq.q: Can you visit the Sacred Valley on the way to Machu Picchu?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely a popular and efficient route — many visitors stop here before catching the train onward to Machu Picchu from Ollantaytambo.
